email.subject: Your parcel is waitting !!! pay the small fee

body.v: Your parcle is held at our depot. You must payed a small fee of CHF 2.50 todday or it will be send back.
Thank you for you patiense and have a nice day.

hotspots.explain: A free mailbox, not parcelpoint.example. A carrier writes from its own domain, not from a throwaway address.
"Dear costumer": no name, and a mistake in the very first words. The carrier you have an account with knows what you're called.
"todday or it will be send back": a deadline of a few hours, so you pay before you think.
The button leads to an unknown address, on a domain that has nothing to do with ParcelPoint.
More mistakes, right down to the sign-off. Companies proofread their messages; a scammer in a hurry rarely does.

who.prompt: Who is really writing to you? Read the address, not just the name.
who.answer: Not ParcelPoint. The address is on free-mailbox.example instead of parcelpoint.example, and no carrier sends a message riddled with mistakes.
choices: A stranger using a free mailbox
A neighbour who took in your parcel

emotion.prompt: Which feeling is this email pressing on?
emotion.answer: Hurry: pay today, or the parcel goes back.
choices: None: it's a simple delivery notice

ask.prompt: What does it actually want you to do?
ask.answer: Pay a fee through the link. The payment page would collect your card details.
choices: Collect the parcel from a neighbour
Pay a fee through the link

verify.prompt: How can you check through a channel you control?
verify.answer: Leave the link alone. Open the ParcelPoint app yourself, or type its address, and look at your current deliveries.
choices: Pay the small fee, just in case
Reply and ask for another link

actions.label: Open the ParcelPoint app yourself and check your deliveries
actions.consequence: No parcel on hold, nothing to pay. The email was fake, and you gave nothing away.

actions.label: Pay the fee through the link
actions.consequence: Your card details go to the scammer. The small fee was only a pretext: now they can charge far more.

actions.label: Report the email as phishing, then delete it
actions.consequence: Nothing was clicked, and your email provider gets better at spotting the next one.

attacker_reveal: Three typos a line, a throwaway address and a fee too small to bother questioning. I made no effort at all. People waiting for a parcel pay anyway.
